notes: Orban OPTIMOD 8700i is a discontinued FM/HD/streaming broadcast audio processor (replaced by OPTIMOD 5950); spec sourced from manufacturer's own specifications page. AES3 ports are physically XLR-type connectors per Orban's spec text but mapped to the "aes3" connector id (distinct from analog "xlr3") since digital AES3 XLR is a separate enum option. GPI is a DB-25 male 8-channel opto-isolated interface, not a true RS-232 port; DB-25/DB-9 are not in the allowed connector-id list so both GPI and the three DB-9 serial ports were mapped to "rs232" as the closest available id. Dante/AES67 link speed (100Mb vs Gigabit) is not published by Orban or by the Dante compatibility listing, so grade was omitted for those two RJ45 ports. No grade applies to AES3 (192kHz composite) since AES3 has no entry in the required grade scale. Corroborating detail pulled from orban.com "In-depth description" and "Key features" pages and getdante.com's Orban 8700i listing.

ports.name: Dante/AES67 Primary
ports.note: AoIP, 2 stereo in / 2 stereo out (4x4), dual-redundant with Secondary; link speed not stated by manufacturer

ports.name: Dante/AES67 Secondary
ports.note: Redundant AoIP link, paired with Primary; link speed not stated by manufacturer

ports.name: Digital Composite (MPX) Out
ports.note: 192 kHz AES3 composite baseband output, delivered on a breakout cable

ports.name: GPI
ports.note: Actual connector is DB-25 male, 8 opto-isolated GPI inputs; DB-25 not in the allowed list, mapped to closest D-sub serial/control id
